rationale: This is a mechanical stacking of three already-tested refinements (capacity normalization, IND_RANK quality, burn indicator) that individually produced near-identical statistics (alpha ~3.1–3.3%, t ~2.6–2.8) and are almost certainly highly collinear, so it offers no new economic mechanism and its outcome will be uninterpretable as to which element matters.

The stated motivation collapses under its own numbers — the two measurement routes already cover 0.079 and 0.084 and both legs still require oancf for the quality weight, so the union can add at most a percent or two of sample, making this a data-plumbing patch rather than an economically motivated signal.

This is the archive's "Cash-burn amplified stress kink" with RANK swapped for IND_RANK (or equivalently the "Peer-relative quality" kink plus the burn dummy), a two-knob recombination of components already tested at t≈2.6–2.84, and its value as an ablation of Proposal 1 does not make it a substantively different hypothesis.

Substituting MA(3) for the one-year oancf weight inside an otherwise unchanged incumbent kink is a single smoothing-parameter tweak, not a new interaction, and the archive already shows that smoothing the quality weight (and the flow) in this family degrades rather than improves alpha.

Assigning different measurement horizons to the payout and issuance legs is a genuinely structural asymmetry with a defensible rationale (programme-like buybacks vs. event-like raises), but the construction is flawed in that the two indicators no longer partition the sample — a firm with MA<0 and current-year raise loads on both legs while the reverse case loads on neither — so results will be partly driven by that overlap rather than by horizon per se.

Weighting the payout leg by funding capacity (costly-signalling) and the issuance leg by earnings opacity (adverse selection) is an economically coherent, leg-specific pairing that is distinct from both the symmetric earnings-stability kink and the symmetric uncertainty amplifier in the archive, and it offers a testable diagnosis of why the latter had a strong FMB slope but negligible alpha.
